items.title: Fed Holds, Warsh Dovishly Points Away From Hikes
items.summary: The Fed held rates steady, as expected, but a surprise came with Warsh's dovish suggestion that he's watching a “broader range” of inflation metrics and that markets may have already done the work of tightening conditions. We continue to expect rate cuts in October, December and January.

items.title: We're Raising Our Microsoft Estimates and Target Price
items.summary: Microsoft’s strong 4Q26 results offered a solid rebuttal to the bear case, with broad-based upside across revenue, earnings, and guidance. Azure and Copilot were standout drivers, while profitability and efficiency improved. We raise our FY27 estimates and lift our target price to $600.

items.title: Japan Equity Strategy: Tech Adjustment in Final Phase
items.summary: Tech stocks corrected sharply from late June, with the Nikkei falling from its highs. Yet high-beta sectors performed well and TOPIX was flat, suggesting broader risk aversion hasn't intensified. Additional downside looks limited, and we still expect a tech-led bull market by year-end.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: The Fed Wants It Steeper
items.summary: Markets may sell some USD in the near term if the Fed stays on hold. Short-term noise doesn’t eradicate our theory of a medium-term U.S.-Iran compromise. We believe the Fed will be comfortable to keep rates unchanged throughout the year. In equities, value continues to outperform growth.

items.title: China Economics: Rate Cut Green Light, Fiscal Acceleration Ahead
items.summary: The Politburo convened its mid-year meeting today to discuss economic issues. The readout came in broadly in line with our expectations — stronger policy rhetoric, but light on specific actions. We summarize our takeaways in this note.

items.title: We're Upgrading Ford to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading Ford to Buy, as we see a turnabout in momentum for the company. Accelerating production of the F-series, lower warranty accruals, an improved aluminum supply and moderating material costs are all positive signs for 2026's second half. We offer further analysis within.

items.title: The Speculative Grade Beat: Reversing Our AI Recommendation
items.summary: Our January overweight call on AI delivered, as AI returned 8.5% against the index's 2.6% through June. But the picture changed in July as AI lagged by nearly 300 basis points, revealing more fragility than headlines initially suggested. We reverse our recommendation to underweight.

items.title: Seagate Delivers a Beat & Raise Quarter
items.summary: Seagate delivered better-than-expected results and guidance, as demand remains exceptionally strong from hyperscalers, AI workloads and growing data retention and a number of factors continue to drive margin expansion. We raise our target price on Buy-rated STX to $1,300.

items.title: Visa Sees Value-Added Services Growth Separating Itself
items.summary: Visa delivered another quarter marked by broad-based outperformance: Consumer spending remained resilient and we particularly note continued acceleration in Value-Added Services. Indications point to FY27 as another strong year above recent growth rates; we raise our target price to $440.

items.title: U.S. Equity Strategy: AI’s Subtle S&P 500 Impacts
items.summary: Our “cluster” approach to aligning the S&P 500 per Growth, Cyclical and Defensive components raises important index considerations, as explored herein. Overall, the underlying AI influence on U.S. equities is testing conventional investment perspectives and asset-allocation decisions.

items.title: Cadence Design Systems' Revenue Momentum Looks Set to Continue
items.summary: Cadence Design Systems reported a solid beat-and-raise quarter and raised FY26 revenue guidance to $6.30 billion, up 19% year-over-year. We see revenue momentum extending through 2027 and so raise our EPS estimates and increase our target price for Buy-rated CDNS to $420.

items.title: Quantitative Global Macro Strategy: Selectively Concentrated
items.summary: Asset allocators remain pro-risk but increasingly selective and concentrated. Under the hood, investors retain conviction in AI-led growth while diversifying away from expensive, concentrated U.S. exposure. In this note we also analyze the macro picture and consider other asset classes.

items.title: The High-Grade Beat: Hyperscaler High Tide
items.summary: The year-to-date widening from hyperscalers appears fair for a supply-and-technical adjustment rather than fundamental deterioration. As AI exposure quietly extends past 40% of the index, issuer and structure-level discrimination is where the next round of risk and reward will be decided.

items.title: Global Gas and Power Insights: Reassessing EU Storage
items.summary: Fundamentally, the recent JKM and TTF price surge was stretched unless the Strait of Hormuz is closed through the third quarter and into the fourth. While the market’s concern about Europe’s ability to refill storage is directionally right, the magnitude appears stretched to us.

items.title: North America Internet: Second-Quarter Preview
items.summary: We preview second-quarter earnings for Reddit, Pinterest, Snap, Carvana and DoorDash. In general, we expect healthier digital-ad spending and note rising engagement metrics; we review specific factors at play for each of the five names at hand and offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: U.S. Financial Software: Second-Quarter Preview
items.summary: We're cautiously optimistic about second-quarter financial-software earnings given the sector's valuation reset. Investor focus will center on second-half pipeline opportunities, AI monetization, and signs of accelerating growth. We review our preferred names in this note.

items.title: Africa Weekly: A Look at Zambia's Upcoming Elections
items.summary: In this edition we consider the upcoming elections in Zambia and their potential policy implications, then examine recent trends in the Zambian kwacha and the outlook for the currency.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: FOMC Premiums and Treasury Refunding Preview
items.summary: We remain received into the Fed meeting despite the rise in risk premium. In our view, there's no compelling reason to drive policymakers toward a hike. We also discuss opportunities across both linear and non-linear expressions into the meeting, and preview the August Treasury refunding.

items.title: Emerging Markets Economic Outlook & Strategy: The Growth Divide
items.summary: There are only a few potential emerging-markets winners in the U.S.-led AI capex cycle, but if the 1990s IT revolution is any guide, future productivity gains could accrue more to users than producers. Here too, emerging markets look relatively disadvantaged vs. developed ones.

items.title: Global Asset Allocation: House Views July 2026
items.summary: The Middle East conflict has escalated again, with oil recovering much of its June losses. Rates have taken their cues from oil, while equities and FX have remained more stable. We remain overweight equities, as we still expect an eventual conflict resolution, but the size is reduced.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Earnings Get an Asterisk
items.summary: Consensus S&P 500 earnings for 2026 have surged past our high-on-the-Street $350 estimate — thus the asterisk. We also look at factors follow-through price action must contend with, and the lingering question of capex persistence for the AI-affected part of the market.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Constraints Vs. Capabilities
items.summary: The realized risk from autonomous agents escaping sandboxes creates new fault lines around security and regulation while open-weight models proliferate and grow more performant. We also look at why token spend will continue to accelerate, driving an increasing demand for infrastructure.

items.title: FX Basis Quarterly: Could the Fed Meeting Jeopardize the Basis?
items.summary: The XCCY basis could experience widening pressure if the Fed hikes. While this isn't our base case, the market’s introduction of front-end risk premium could slow down carry trades. We offer further analysis herein and discuss next year’s debt ceiling, which should support our position.

items.title: U.S. Semiconductors & Semi Equipment: Analyzing a Summer Sell-Off
items.summary: We view the SOX pullback as a buying opportunity. Fundamentally, data centers remain the strongest end market at 34% of semis' total addressable market, and look on track to exceed the entire semis TAM by 2030. We recap key earnings highlights and discuss why we prefer semi caps to semis.

items.title: Intel's Transformation Shows Signs of Progress
items.summary: Intel reported its strongest revenue growth in more than 15 years, with most-recent results and EPS outlook both well above consensus. INTC is benefiting from agentic AI-driven double-digit server CPU unit growth, and we see signs of confidence in its external foundry business.

items.title: Edwards Lifesciences Emerges As a MedTech Unicorn
items.summary: Edwards Lifesciences reported better-than-expected results and raised guidance. Overall, management noted “confidence in our target of ~10%” sales growth: and the second quarter certainly creates a line of sight to that. We reiterate our Buy on EW and offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: North America Hardware & Storage: We're Raising Two Target Prices
items.summary: On the heels of AMD’s Analyst Day and Intel results, we're raising expectations for Dell and HPE. We're more convinced that enterprise IT infrastructure spending continues to strengthen, supported by ongoing AI-related investments, server refresh cycles and broader data-center demand.

items.title: U.S. Airlines:  A Second-Quarter EPS Update
items.summary: We're updating airlines' EPS estimates and price targets. Rising fuel prices have made company guidance stale almost upon release. In many cases, we now see downside to second-half consensus EPS estimates, though our 2027/28 EPS estimates are ultimately little changed for most names.

items.title: ASEAN Telcos Deserve Another Look Given the Broadening Debate
items.summary: ASEAN telcos have broadly underperformed this year given investors' preference for higher-beta sectors and markets and some now offer attractive relative value, backed by positive operating momentum, mobile-pricing trends and cost-cutting initiatives. We review our preferred names herein.

items.title: Global Precious Metals & Minerals: First-Half Earnings Preview
items.summary: We expect significant year-over-year earnings increases for global precious-metal equities primarily due to higher PGM and gold prices, which we believe are well embedded into market expectations. We see solid balance sheets for the sector, and review what we think investors will focus on.

items.title: Mexico Economics Weekly: USMCA's Third Round Isn't a Charm Yet
items.summary: The lack of a USMCA breakthrough so far supports our view that trade negotiations are likely to extend into 2026. We still think Mexico, the U.S. and Canada ultimately extend their trade deal, but the uncertainties suggest a downside bias to our 2% GDP growth forecast for 2027.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: The Cracks Are Showing
items.summary: In the absence of second-round inflationary effects, energy prices will continue to be the main driver of € monetary policy, and we recommend buying short-expiry vs. intermediate vol on front-end rates. We preview the Bank of England's upcoming meeting and offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Global Economic Outlook & Strategy: Uncertainties and Resilience
items.summary: Higher oil prices have taken a bite out of the global economy's performance, but the pain has stayed manageable amid continued resilience. We're more sanguine about growth for the rest of the year, as the reality is that the global economy is less dependent on oil than in previous decades.

items.title: Foreign Exchange Forecasts: July 2026
items.summary: We leave our near-term EURUSD forecast unchanged at 1.13 to reflect USD-positive asymmetry around the Fed’s reaction function and the U.S.-Iran conflict. G10 RV trades look increasingly attractive, though, and we forecast upside in EURGBP and NOKSEK, alongside downside in AUDNZD.

items.title: Global Commodities: Wildcards for 2026's Second Half
items.summary: Geopolitical, climate and technological shocks routinely overwhelm traditional supply-demand analysis for commodities, so investors need to consider plausible events that markets are least prepared for. We look at nine potential commodities wildcards for 2026's second half and beyond.
